QUESTIONS I KEEP COMING BACK TO

Memory. Autonomy. Knowledge that lasts.

Short- & long-term memoryEarned autonomyReusable team knowledge

Memory needs boundaries.

I want to explore short- and long-term agent memory: what to retain, forget, or ask permission to reuse. Useful personalization needs ownership and correction paths.

Autonomy should be earned.

Which steps can run unattended, and what evidence would justify more freedom? I would expand autonomy only after task-level evals and reviewable records.

Knowledge should compound.

How can a team turn resolved exceptions into reusable knowledge without letting unverified answers become the next source of truth?

INDUSTRY LENS & CAREER FOCUS

The AI product questions
I want to own.

My view: useful AI products need a reliable path from answers to actions. Technical AI PM work means defining the job, the evidence of success, and the limits of autonomy—not just selecting a model.

01 / SCOPE

What should the system own?

Separate answering from acting. Define the job, the tools, and the point where a person must decide.

02 / EVIDENCE

What counts as a good outcome?

Evaluate the task, attribute failures to a system stage, and compare quality with latency and cost.

03 / CONTROL

Can a decision be reviewed?

Keep sources, approvals, and action records visible. Make a proposal easy to inspect before it becomes an irreversible action.

Seeking technical AI PM roles; open to AI engineering-adjacent roles.

Propose→Approve→Record

A human still decides; nothing irreversible happens without a named person.

Services and method examples↓

Agent product design

A written job spec: who sits in the seat, what arrives, what “done” looks like, and the gate the agent cannot cross.

Agent build

The first seat ships. The agent may draft, retrieve, route, classify, and queue; nothing irreversible without a named person.

Agent operations

Evals against the job, not a generic model scoreboard. Tighten the gate where the workflow still fails; improve the record so a proposal can be reopened.

Four desks. One method.

Four illustrations of the method, not four client engagements.

Demand desk

A high-touch demand desk: an occasion maps to one hero product, a try-on still, and a drafted bag.

A human stands before pay.
Knowledge desk

A controller desk that answers from a fixed corpus, attaches citations, and drafts a Propose package.

A human stands before any corpus change.
Attention desk

An operator desk that sorts Priority / Watch / Noise, drafts in two tones, and escalates.

A human stands before send.
Exception desk

An ops desk that ranks the exception queue, suggests a policy disposition, and drafts the case note.

A human stands before money moves.

DESIGN THINKING APPLIED TO PAST WORK

What I would improve next.

Proposed extensions to independent projects—not shipped features.

SpringCloud e-commerce platform

Better search, with the same permission boundary.

Starting point: Elasticsearch product search, a Keycloak-backed BFF, and Debezium CDC.

Design question: Could image-and-text search improve product discovery while keeping catalog updates consistent and order actions behind the existing service permissions?

How I would test it: Compare relevance, stale-result rate, latency, and permission failures against the existing text-search path.

Twitter analytics platform

Make freshness and provenance visible.

Starting point: Spark ETL, MySQL/HBase storage, Redis caching, and distributed tracing.

Design question: If a source-grounded assistant queried these analytics, how would it expose data timestamps and invalidate cached answers when source data changes?

How I would test it: Replay delayed updates and cache invalidation failures; check answer provenance, freshness, and response time.

HOW I THINKA REUSABLE FRAMEWORK

Start with the question.
Make the reasoning visible.

A good architecture connects a product objective to decisions that can be inspected and tested.

  1. Clarify requirements
  2. Define LLM objectives
  3. Draw system boundaries
  4. Design the architecture
  5. Evaluate
  6. Ship with trade-offs

Architecture follows the problem: RAG, agents, multimodal systems, reasoning — or a combination.

01

Autonomy is a design choice.

Workflow vs. agent: choose the right level of autonomy. Design tool use, state, human review, fallback, and escalation together.

02

Evals come first.

Define what “good” looks like, build an eval dataset, find which stage fails, and test whether a change actually improves the product.

03

Decisions need evidence.

Every architecture choice names the alternatives considered and why each was or was not chosen. Make the trade-offs reviewable.

A SHARED DECISION PROCESS

How I work with PMs and engineers.

Turn ambiguous requirements into architecture decisions that a team can evaluate, discuss, and revise.

  1. Frame the product question.Clarify user needs, constraints, success criteria, and the cost of getting it wrong.
  2. Make alternatives reviewable.Map system boundaries and compare options with explicit assumptions and trade-offs.
  3. Agree on evidence.Define evaluation cases, ownership, release gates, and escalation before increasing autonomy.
